Consider the following PR description:
FileInput shouldn't display required attribute when initial data exists.
Description
	 
		(last modified by thenewguy)
	 
I think that ClearableFileInput.use_required_attribute() (​https://github.com/django/django/blob/e703b93a656b78b9b444bb3a9980e305ed002a70/django/forms/widgets.py#L454) should be moved to FileInput.use_required_attribute() so that required is not output on the html input element that represents FileInput when a file is already set (e.g. already saved on a model instance that is being edited).
Maybe I am overlooking a use case where this is not desirable? I can not think of one.

</pr_description>

Now I understand the issue. Currently:
- `FileInput` does not have its own `use_required_attribute` method, so it inherits from `Widget` (via `Input`)
- `ClearableFileInput` has `use_required_attribute` that checks if there's initial data and returns `False` when there is

The PR description suggests moving the `use_required_attribute` logic from `ClearableFileInput` to `FileInput` so that the `required` attribute is not shown on the HTML input element when a file is already set for a regular `FileInput` as well (not just `ClearableFileInput`).

Now I understand:

1. `ClearableFileInput` has a test `test_use_required_attribute` that shows:
   - Returns `True` when there's no initial data (None)
   - Returns `False` when there's initial data ('resume.txt')

2. The logic in `ClearableFileInput.use_required_attribute` is: `return super().use_required_attribute(initial) and not initial`

According to the PR description, this same logic should be moved to `FileInput` so that the `required` attribute is not shown when a file is already set for any file input widget, not just `ClearableFileInput`.
